title: The Biggest Bomb Ever Shattered Windows 560 Miles Away

scenes.text: The biggest bomb ever tested shattered windows 560 miles away.
October 1961. The Soviet Tsar Bomba. 50 megatons. 1,570 times Hiroshima and Nagasaki combined.
The mushroom cloud climbed 40 miles. Seven Everests, stacked.
A village 34 miles away was wiped flat. Windows broke in Norway and Finland.
The shockwave went around the Earth three times. Seismometers felt the third lap.
It was designed for 100 megatons. They cut it in half to limit the fallout. This was the small version.

description:
On October 30, 1961, the Soviet Union detonated the Tsar Bomba over Novaya Zemlya: about 50 megatons, roughly 1,570 times the Hiroshima and Nagasaki bombs combined.
The mushroom cloud rose about 40 miles, every building in a village 34 miles away was destroyed, windows shattered as far as 560 miles away in Norway and Finland, and the shockwave was recorded circling the Earth three times.
Should a weapon this big ever have been built?
first_comment: One witness felt the heat on his face from 170 miles away, through dark goggles. Which number in this video shocked you most?
